explanation: In the 1400s Venice made ships from plague-hit ports wait quaranta giorni, forty days, before anyone could land. Other Mediterranean ports copied the rule.

claims.text: 'Quarantine' comes from Venetian Italian quaranta giorni, 'forty days'.
The source of 'quarantine' refers to neither 14, 30 nor 100 days.
In the 15th century Venice required ships from plague-affected ports to wait 40 days before passengers and crew could land.
Other Mediterranean ports adopted similar waiting rules for ships.
